name: Transmembrane Signal Transduction: GPCRs, Second Messengers, and Receptor Tyrosine Kinases

reference.source: Medical Biochemistry 5th ed / Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry 8th ed
clinicalPearls: G-alpha-s stimulates adenylyl cyclase to elevate cAMP and activate Protein Kinase A; G-alpha-i inhibits this pathway
G-alpha-q activates phospholipase C-beta, hydrolyzing PIP2 into IP3 (releasing ER Ca2+) and DAG (activating PKC)
Receptor tyrosine kinases dimerize and autophosphorylate, recruiting Grb2-SOS to activate the Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK cascade
Inactivating GNAS mutations cause pseudohypoparathyroidism 1A with Albright hereditary osteodystrophy
Post-zygotic activating GNAS mutations cause McCune-Albright syndrome (fibrous dysplasia, cafe-au-lait, precocious puberty)
reference.pathophysiology: Extracellular hormones and growth factors engage cell surface receptors to transduce intracellular cascades. Heterotrimeric G-proteins cycle between GDP-bound inactive and GTP-bound active states. Inactivating GNAS mutations impair G-alpha-s coupling, conferring end-organ resistance to PTH and TSH. Somatic activating GNAS mutations produce constitutive adenylyl cyclase activation, driving autonomous endocrine hypersecretion and skeletal fibrous dysplasia.
additionalInvestigations: Serum calcium, phosphate, and intact PTH levels (elevated PTH with hypocalcemia in PHP)
Urinary cyclic AMP excretion in response to exogenous PTH infusion (Ellsworth-Howard test)
Skeletal survey and bone scan for polyostotic fibrous dysplasia
Targeted GNAS gene mutation analysis from peripheral blood or affected tissue
